subject: reasoning
question:
Rajat drove 4 km west from point A. He turned left and drove 4 km. He again turned left and drove 8 km and then he turned right and drove 3 km. Then, he turned right and drove 4 km. Finally, he turned right and drove 6 km and stopped at point B.

How far (shortest distance) and in which direction should he drive to reach point A again?

(All turns are 90° turns only, unless specified.)
solution:
Given:

From place A, Rajat drives 4 km towards the West.

He then turned left and drove for 4 km.

He turned left and drove 8 km and then turned right and drove 3 km.

He then turned right and drove for 4 km.

In the end, he turned right, drove for 6 km and stopped at place B. 

Based on the given conditions, we get the following direction distance diagram as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35b6c315dbc4ff1c42a4c169413d054b986cf6d1a8b1ffcc1250cdeba5681032.png] 

Therefore, in order to go back to place A again, he has to drive 1 km towards the North. 

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option 2**".
